demos.question: Can APC mutation analysis contribute to therapeutic decisions in familial adenomatous polyposis?
demos.answer:
APC mutation analysis has been extensively studied in the context of familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), a genetic disorder characterized by the development of hundreds to thousands of polyps in the colon and rectum. While the primary treatment for FAP involves surgical removal of the colon and rectum, APC mutation analysis can provide valuable information for therapeutic decisions.

In patients with FAP who develop intra-abdominal desmoid tumors, APC mutation analysis can help identify potential genetic mutations that may contribute to the development of these tumors [1]. This information can be used to guide treatment decisions, such as the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or other medications to prevent the growth of desmoid tumors.

Furthermore, APC mutation analysis can also be used to identify patients with FAP who are at increased risk of developing other cancers, such as breast cancer. For example, studies have shown that certain single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) at different loci are associated with breast cancer susceptibility, and that these SNPs can be used to improve the predictive ability of risk models [2].

In addition, APC mutation analysis can be used to diagnose FAP in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding, which is a common symptom of the disease. A study using double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) found that APC mutation analysis was useful in diagnosing FAP in patients with obscure gastrointestinal bleeding, with a diagnostic yield of 75% [3].

However, the impact of APC mutation analysis on therapeutic decisions in FAP patients is not well understood. A study of 330 patients with FAP found that younger patients had a worse estimated 5-year disease-free survival rate, but this did not retain significance when analyzed by stage [4]. This suggests that APC mutation analysis may not have a significant impact on therapeutic decisions in FAP patients.

In conclusion, while APC mutation analysis can provide valuable information for therapeutic decisions in FAP patients, its impact on treatment outcomes is not well understood. Further studies are needed to determine the clinical utility of APC mutation analysis in FAP patients.
